title: A radical ideal with prime-generated minimal primes is principal
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is an integral domain, meaning $1\ne0$ and a product is zero only if one factor is zero. Let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Assume $I$ is radical: if $a^m\in I$ for $a\in R$ and an integer $m\geq1$, then $a\in I$. A prime ideal means a proper ideal $\mathfrak q$ such that $ab\in\mathfrak q$ implies $a\in\mathfrak q$ or $b\in\mathfrak q$. A prime ideal minimal over $I$ means a prime ideal containing $I$ with no strictly smaller prime ideal containing $I$. Suppose that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q$ minimal over $I$ there is a prime element $\pi\in R$ such that $\mathfrak q=(\pi)$. Here a prime element is nonzero, is not a unit, and divides a product only if it divides one of the factors; $(\pi)=\{\pi r:r\in R\}$. Then there is $f\in R$, $f\ne0$, with $I=(f)$. The case $I=R$ is allowed, with its condition on minimal primes vacuous.
